fatal_errors: The claim that grain-boundary transport to the external surface governs protection is not directly established by the cited evidence; E2 reports grain-boundary-promoted internal Al oxidation and substantial BCC/B2-to-FCC transformation.

The proposed fine-grained versus coarse-grained comparison does not isolate grain-boundary density because grain refinement processing can also alter phase constitution, defects, surface energy, and elemental partitioning.
explanation: The hypothesis is scientifically plausible and testable, and it correctly invokes selective Al/Cr oxidation and slow-growing alumina/chromia as protective barriers. It is not a reconstruction of the target study, however. The target varied oxygen availability during an in-situ ramp to 1100 °C and attributed the air–vacuum difference primarily to oxygen-dependent selective outward diffusion and consumption of Al, followed by Cr, with associated substrate phase transformations and Al-depleted subsurface zones. The generated hypothesis instead makes grain-boundary density the governing variable and proposes an isothermal fine-versus-coarse-grain comparison. E2 supports improved oxidation kinetics after microstructural refinement, but does not uniquely support outward grain-boundary delivery to an external scale, while E1 concerns Mn-dominated, non-protective oxidation in a different alloy. The proposed measurements are useful, though tracer diffusion, depth-resolved composition, and controls matching phase constitution and processing defects would be needed to distinguish grain-boundary transport from correlated microstructural effects.
